### Summary

Two deck keys under `integration`[^rg-8af4d8f27442] choose how a block's stages run. `execution` takes `auto`, `eager` or
`cuda-graph`, and `auto` is the default, also when the key is absent: a block whose coordinates live on a CUDA
device runs cuda-graph, any other block runs eager. An explicit value is followed as written. In cuda-graph mode a
refused case or segment runs eager and is logged (@sec-ch11-refusals). `execution-strict` turns that fallback into
an error: a strict case that cannot be captured stops before its first launch and names the first eager segment
and its reasons. Strict needs cuda-graph (or `auto`, which strict resolves to cuda-graph); `eager` with strict is
refused when the deck is read, as an eager case is never refused.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Choose eager or graph execution per block, and whether a refusal is an error.

**Data.** Reads `integration/execution` and `integration/execution-strict` from the deck, and the device of the
block's coordinates.

**Placement.** Read once when the deck is parsed; resolved at every stage by `StageExecutor::mode`.

**Activation.** `execution: auto | eager | cuda-graph` (default `auto`); `execution-strict: true | false` (default
`false`).

**Guarantee / limits.** `auto` captures on CUDA and never on the CPU; an explicit `eager` is never captured. A
strict case either captures every non-host segment or stops before launching anything.

**Evidence.** `test_default_execution_python`, `test_execution_capability_python` (@tbl-ch11-default-tests).
:::

Local symbols of this section: none.

### Derivation

None: two rules. The mode of a block is

| `execution` | `execution-strict` | block on CUDA | mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `eager` | false | any | eager |
| `eager` | true | any | refused when the deck is read |
| `cuda-graph` | any | any | cuda-graph (on the CPU: every stage refused, so eager or, with strict, an error) |
| `auto` | true | any | cuda-graph |
| `auto` | false | yes | cuda-graph |
| `auto` | false | no | eager |

: The mode of `StageExecutor::mode` ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::mode >}}) and the deck
check of `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
{#tbl-ch11-default-mode}

and in cuda-graph mode a non-empty reason list runs eager without strict and stops the run with it.

### Numerical method

**Reading the keys.** `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads both keys from the `integration` node, checks that
`execution` is one of the three values ("integration/execution must be auto, eager or cuda-graph") and refuses
strict with `eager`. The defaults are in the options class
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.hpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl >}}).

**Strict.** `StageExecutor::check_strict` ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::check_strict >}})
runs before any launch: in `run_stage` for a bare block and, for a Mesh, on the calling thread for every block
before any block starts (`MeshImpl::forward`). It skips host segments, which are boundaries, and stops at the
first segment with a reason: "integration/execution-strict: this case cannot run as a CUDA graph: segment *i*
(*ops*) of block *b*, stage *s* runs eager:" followed by the reasons, one per line.

### Code

**How to use it.**

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `type`[^rg-6776b325d30c].
```yaml
integration:
  type: rk3
  execution: auto          # auto (default), eager or cuda-graph
  execution-strict: false  # true: refuse a case that cannot be captured
```

To compare a run with its eager twin, set `execution: eager` on one copy of the deck; the two must agree bit for
bit (@sec-ch11-graphsafe).

**What is refused, and why.** An unknown `execution` value, and `execution: eager` with `execution-strict: true`,
when the deck is read. With strict, any case or segment with a reason, before the first launch.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `auto` follows the device of the block's coordinates; a block built on the CPU and moved later resolves its
  mode from where its coordinates are at each stage.
- Without strict, a refusal is a warning printed once per block and reason; a long run's log can hide it.
:::
